limitations_and_boundaries: The study primarily uses immortalized fibroblast lines, which may not fully recapitulate primary CAF biology.
The in vivo experiments are limited to subcutaneous matrix plug assays and do not assess orthotopic tumour growth or metastasis.
The mechanism of YAP activation by Src and actomyosin does not involve changes in MST1/2 or S127-YAP phosphorylation, but the precise molecular link remains unclear.
The feedback loop model is based on in vitro and plug assays; its relevance to spontaneous tumour progression in vivo requires further validation.
The study focuses on breast and squamous cell carcinoma CAFs; generalizability to other cancer types is not addressed.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

methods.name: Fibroblast isolation and immortalization
methods.protocol_description: Fibroblasts were isolated from MMTV-PyMT mouse mammary tissue at different stages (normal, hyperplasia, adenoma, carcinoma) and immortalized using HPV-E6 retrovirus.

methods.name: Immunofluorescence microscopy
methods.protocol_description: Cells were seeded on collagen I/Matrigel matrix, fixed, permeabilized, and stained with antibodies against vimentin, αSMA, F-actin, paxillin, fibronectin, and DAPI.

methods.name: Western blotting
methods.protocol_description: Protein lysates from cells on collagen I/Matrigel were analyzed by SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting with antibodies against αSMA, fibronectin, S100A4, pS19-MYL9, MYL9, MYH9, MYH10, DIAPH1, and tubulin.

methods.name: Gel contraction assay
methods.protocol_description: 75×10^3 fibroblasts were embedded in 100 µl collagen I/Matrigel; gel contraction was measured after 3 days by comparing gel diameter to well diameter.

methods.name: Atomic force microscopy (AFM)
methods.protocol_description: Elastic modulus of fibroblast-remodelled collagen I/Matrigel gels was measured using AFM with a 35-µm-radius glass bead tip; force-distance curves were fitted to a Hertz contact model.

methods.name: Organotypic invasion assay
methods.protocol_description: Fibroblasts were embedded in collagen I/Matrigel; after 16 h, 5×10^5 4T1 cancer cells were seeded on top and covered with a thin gel layer; cultures were maintained for 6 days, then fixed and stained for H&E; invasion index was calculated as 1−(non-invading area/total area).

methods.name: In vivo matrix plug angiogenesis assay
methods.protocol_description: Fibroblasts were embedded in collagen I/Matrigel plugs and injected subcutaneously into mice; after 7 days, plugs were harvested, sectioned, and stained for endomucin and vimentin; angiogenesis was quantified as endomucin staining relative to vimentin-positive fibroblast number.

methods.name: Microarray analysis
methods.protocol_description: Gene expression profiles of NFs and CAFs were compared using microarrays; differentially expressed genes were identified and validated by qPCR.

methods.name: qPCR
methods.protocol_description: RNA was extracted, reverse transcribed, and analyzed by quantitative real-time PCR using gene-specific primers; expression was normalized to Lamc2 or Gapdh.

methods.name: YAP/TAZ localization analysis
methods.protocol_description: Cells or tissue sections were stained for YAP/TAZ, F-actin, and DAPI; nuclear localization was quantified as percentage of cells with predominant nuclear staining or by nuclear/cytosolic intensity ratio.

methods.name: siRNA transfection
methods.protocol_description: CAFs were transfected with siRNA smart pools or individual siRNAs targeting YAP, TAZ, or other genes using standard protocols; knockdown efficiency was confirmed by western blot or qPCR.
